title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03) - Basic

summary.description: Covers design of resilient, high-performing, secure, and cost-optimized AWS solutions.

questions.question: A company hosts a web application in multiple Availability Zones (AZs) and wants to ensure high availability. Which approach provides the best fault tolerance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use a single EC2 instance in one AZ.
choices.explanation: Incorrect — lacks high availability and fault tolerance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use an Auto Scaling group spanning multiple AZs.
choices.explanation: Correct — ensures redundancy and fault tolerance across multiple AZs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use a single EC2 instance with EBS snapshots.
choices.explanation: Incorrect — snapshots don't provide real-time high availability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use multiple EC2 instances in the same AZ.
choices.explanation: Incorrect — single AZ failure would affect all instances.

questions.question: Which AWS service should be used to implement fine-grained access control for S3 buckets?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IAM policies only
choices.explanation: Incorrect — IAM policies alone don't provide bucket-level access control.

choices.label: B
choices.text: S3 bucket policies and IAM policies
choices.explanation: Correct — combination provides comprehensive access control.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Security groups
choices.explanation: Incorrect — security groups are for EC2 instances, not S3.

choices.label: D
choices.text: NACLs only
choices.explanation: Incorrect — NACLs are for VPC subnets, not S3 access control.

questions.question: A company needs to store frequently accessed data with sub-millisecond latency. Which storage solution is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: S3 Standard
choices.explanation: Incorrect — S3 has higher latency than required.

choices.label: B
choices.text: ElastiCache with Redis
choices.explanation: Correct — in-memory cache provides sub-millisecond latency.

choices.label: C
choices.text: EBS gp3
choices.explanation: Incorrect — EBS has higher latency than in-memory solutions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
choices.explanation: Incorrect — still has S3 latency characteristics.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides the most cost-effective solution for running batch processing jobs that can tolerate interruptions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: On-Demand EC2 instances
choices.explanation: Incorrect — more expensive than Spot instances for interruptible workloads.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Spot EC2 instances
choices.explanation: Correct — up to 90% cost savings for interruptible workloads.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reserved EC2 instances
choices.explanation: Incorrect — not suitable for batch jobs that don't run continuously.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dedicated Hosts
choices.explanation: Incorrect — most expensive option and not suitable for batch processing.

questions.question: A company needs to encrypt data at rest in RDS. Which encryption method provides the strongest security?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Application-level encryption only
choices.explanation: Incorrect — doesn't provide comprehensive data protection.

choices.label: B
choices.text: RDS encryption at rest with AWS KMS
choices.explanation: Correct — provides strong encryption with AWS-managed keys.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Database-level encryption only
choices.explanation: Incorrect — doesn't protect all data layers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No encryption needed for RDS
choices.explanation: Incorrect — encryption is essential for sensitive data.

questions.question: Which AWS service should be used to implement a disaster recovery solution with RTO of 4 hours and RPO of 1 hour?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cross-region snapshots only
choices.explanation: Incorrect — doesn't meet RTO requirements for quick recovery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: AWS Backup with cross-region replication
choices.explanation: Incorrect — may not meet the 4-hour RTO requirement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Multi-AZ deployment with cross-region read replicas
choices.explanation: Correct — provides both high availability and disaster recovery capabilities.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Single-AZ deployment with S3 backups
choices.explanation: Incorrect — doesn't provide adequate disaster recovery.

questions.question: A company wants to optimize costs for a database that has predictable usage patterns. Which pricing model should they choose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: On-Demand pricing
choices.explanation: Incorrect — most expensive option for predictable workloads.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reserved Instances with 1-year term
choices.explanation: Correct — provides significant cost savings for predictable usage.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Spot Instances
choices.explanation: Incorrect — not suitable for databases that need consistent availability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dedicated Hosts
choices.explanation: Incorrect — most expensive option and not cost-optimized.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides the best solution for implementing a content delivery network (CDN) for global users?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Application Load Balancer
choices.explanation: Incorrect — provides load balancing but not global content delivery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: CloudFront
choices.explanation: Correct — AWS's CDN service for global content delivery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Route 53
choices.explanation: Incorrect — DNS service, not a CDN.

choices.label: D
choices.text: API Gateway
choices.explanation: Incorrect — API management service, not a CDN.

questions.question: A company needs to grant cross-account access to an S3 bucket. Which approach provides the most secure solution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create IAM users in the source account and attach S3 policies.
choices.explanation: Incorrect — IAM users don't work across accounts for S3 access.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use S3 bucket policies with cross-account IAM roles.
choices.explanation: Correct — S3 bucket policies combined with cross-account IAM roles provide secure cross-account access.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Share AWS access keys between accounts.
choices.explanation: Incorrect — sharing access keys is a security anti-pattern and not recommended.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use VPC peering to connect the accounts.
choices.explanation: Incorrect — VPC peering is for network connectivity, not S3 access control.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between Security Groups and Network ACLs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Security Groups are stateless, NACLs are stateful.
choices.explanation: Incorrect — it's the opposite: Security Groups are stateful, NACLs are stateless.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Security Groups operate at the instance level, NACLs at the subnet level.
choices.explanation: Correct — Security Groups are attached to instances, NACLs are attached to subnets.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Security Groups only allow traffic, NACLs only deny traffic.
choices.explanation: Incorrect — both can allow and deny traffic, but with different scopes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Security Groups are free, NACLs cost money.
choices.explanation: Incorrect — both are free services, the difference is in their operation level.

questions.question: A company wants to encrypt data at rest in S3 with their own encryption keys. Which option should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: SSE-S3 with AWS-managed keys
choices.explanation: Incorrect — this uses AWS-managed keys, not customer-managed keys.

choices.label: B
choices.text: SSE-KMS with customer-managed CMK
choices.explanation: Correct — SSE-KMS with customer-managed CMK allows the company to control their own encryption keys.

choices.label: C
choices.text: SSE-C with client-side encryption
choices.explanation: Incorrect — SSE-C requires the client to manage keys, not S3.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use S3 Transfer Acceleration
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Transfer Acceleration is for faster uploads, not encryption.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides the most secure way to access EC2 instances without exposing them to the internet?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bastion host in a public subnet
choices.explanation: Incorrect — bastion hosts still require internet access and are less secure than SSM.

choices.label: B
choices.text: SSM Session Manager with VPC endpoints
choices.explanation: Correct — SSM Session Manager provides secure access without internet exposure when using VPC endpoints.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct internet access with security groups
choices.explanation: Incorrect — this exposes instances to the internet, which is not secure.

choices.label: D
choices.text: VPN connection only
choices.explanation: Incorrect — while VPN is secure, SSM Session Manager is more convenient and equally secure.

questions.question: A company needs to implement a disaster recovery solution with RTO of 4 hours and RPO of 1 hour. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pilot light with S3 snapshots
choices.explanation: Incorrect — pilot light typically has longer RTO than 4 hours.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Warm standby with Multi-AZ and cross-region read replicas
choices.explanation: Correct — warm standby with Multi-AZ and read replicas can meet the RTO/RPO requirements.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cold standby with daily backups
choices.explanation: Incorrect — cold standby has much longer RTO and RPO than required.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Active-passive with Route 53 health checks
choices.explanation: Incorrect — this is more complex and expensive than needed for the requirements.

questions.question: Which Auto Scaling policy is best for handling sudden traffic spikes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Target tracking scaling based on CPU utilization
choices.explanation: Correct — target tracking scaling responds quickly to traffic changes and maintains consistent performance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Simple scaling with 5-minute cooldown
choices.explanation: Incorrect — 5-minute cooldown is too slow for sudden traffic spikes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Manual scaling only
choices.explanation: Incorrect — manual scaling cannot respond to sudden traffic spikes automatically.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scheduled scaling based on time
choices.explanation: Incorrect — scheduled scaling cannot handle unexpected traffic spikes.

questions.question: A company wants to optimize Lambda performance and cost. Which approach should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use the maximum memory allocation for all functions
choices.explanation: Incorrect — this would increase costs unnecessarily for functions that don't need high memory.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Right-size memory allocation based on function requirements
choices.explanation: Correct — right-sizing memory allocation optimizes both performance and cost for Lambda functions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use the minimum memory allocation for all functions
choices.explanation: Incorrect — this may cause performance issues for functions that need more memory.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set concurrency limit to 1 for all functions
choices.explanation: Incorrect — this would severely limit performance and throughput.

questions.question: Which EBS volume type provides the best price-performance ratio for general-purpose workloads?

choices.label: A
choices.text: gp2 volumes
choices.explanation: Incorrect — gp2 is older and less cost-effective than gp3.

choices.label: B
choices.text: gp3 volumes
choices.explanation: Correct — gp3 provides better price-performance ratio with baseline performance and ability to provision IOPS and throughput independently.

choices.label: C
choices.text: io1 volumes
choices.explanation: Incorrect — io1 is more expensive and designed for high IOPS workloads, not general-purpose.

choices.label: D
choices.text: st1 volumes
choices.explanation: Incorrect — st1 is for throughput-optimized workloads, not general-purpose.

questions.question: A company wants to improve database read performance. Which caching solution should they implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ElastiCache for Redis with read replicas
choices.explanation: Correct — ElastiCache for Redis provides in-memory caching for frequently accessed data, significantly improving read performance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: S3 with CloudFront for caching
choices.explanation: Incorrect — S3 and CloudFront are for static content, not database caching.

choices.label: C
choices.text: EBS with Provisioned IOPS
choices.explanation: Incorrect — EBS optimization improves storage performance, not database read caching.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Application Load Balancer with sticky sessions
choices.explanation: Incorrect — ALB sticky sessions don't provide database caching functionality.

questions.question: Which service provides the best solution for reducing latency for global users accessing a web application?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AWS Global Accelerator
choices.explanation: Correct — Global Accelerator uses AWS's global network infrastructure to improve performance and availability for global users.

choices.label: B
choices.text: VPC Peering across regions
choices.explanation: Incorrect — VPC peering doesn't reduce latency for end users, it's for connecting VPCs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct Connect
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Direct Connect is for dedicated network connections to AWS, not for reducing end-user latency.

choices.label: D
choices.text: NAT Gateway
choices.explanation: Incorrect — NAT Gateway is for outbound internet access from private subnets, not latency optimization.

questions.question: A company wants to optimize costs for predictable workloads. Which pricing model should they choose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: On-Demand instances
choices.explanation: Incorrect — On-Demand is the most expensive option and not cost-optimized for predictable workloads.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reserved Instances with 1-year term
choices.explanation: Correct — Reserved Instances provide significant cost savings (up to 75%) for predictable workloads with 1-year commitment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Spot Instances for production workloads
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Spot Instances can be interrupted and are not suitable for production workloads.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dedicated Hosts
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Dedicated Hosts are the most expensive option and not cost-optimized.

questions.question: Which approach is most effective for reducing data transfer costs in a multi-region architecture?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use VPC endpoints for S3 access
choices.explanation: Correct — VPC endpoints keep traffic within the AWS network, reducing data transfer costs for S3 access.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use NAT Gateway for all outbound traffic
choices.explanation: Incorrect — NAT Gateway doesn't reduce data transfer costs, it adds costs for data processing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use Direct Connect for all connections
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Direct Connect is expensive and not cost-effective for all data transfer scenarios.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use internet gateway for all traffic
choices.explanation: Incorrect — internet gateway doesn't reduce data transfer costs and may increase them.

questions.question: A company wants to grant an AWS service permission to access resources on their behalf. Which IAM feature should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IAM user with access keys
choices.explanation: Incorrect — IAM users are for human access, not service-to-service access.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Service-linked role
choices.explanation: Correct — service-linked roles are designed for AWS services to access resources on behalf of the customer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cross-account role
choices.explanation: Incorrect — cross-account roles are for accessing resources in different AWS accounts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: IAM group with policies
choices.explanation: Incorrect — IAM groups are for organizing users, not for service access.

questions.question: A company wants to limit the maximum permissions that can be granted to IAM users. Which feature should they implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IAM policies with explicit deny statements
choices.explanation: Incorrect — explicit deny statements don't limit maximum permissions, they just deny specific actions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Permission boundaries
choices.explanation: Correct — permission boundaries define the maximum permissions that can be granted to IAM users and roles.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Resource-based policies
choices.explanation: Incorrect — resource-based policies control access to specific resources, not maximum permissions for users.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Security groups
choices.explanation: Incorrect — security groups are for network access control, not IAM permissions.

questions.question: A company wants to protect their web application from common web attacks. Which AWS service should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AWS Shield Standard
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Shield Standard only provides DDoS protection, not web application protection.

choices.label: B
choices.text: AWS WAF
choices.explanation: Correct — AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) protects web applications from common web exploits and attacks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Security Groups
choices.explanation: Incorrect — security groups control network traffic, not application-layer attacks.

choices.label: D
choices.text: NACLs
choices.explanation: Incorrect — NACLs control subnet-level traffic, not application-layer protection.

questions.question: A company wants to store database credentials securely and rotate them automatically. Which AWS service should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Parameter Store
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Parameter Store can store secrets but doesn't provide automatic rotation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: AWS Secrets Manager
choices.explanation: Correct — AWS Secrets Manager provides automatic rotation for database credentials and other secrets.

choices.label: C
choices.text: S3 with encryption
choices.explanation: Incorrect — S3 can store encrypted data but doesn't provide automatic credential rotation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: KMS with manual rotation
choices.explanation: Incorrect — KMS manages encryption keys, not application secrets or credentials.

questions.question: A company wants to connect their VPC to AWS services without using the internet. Which solution should they implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: VPC Peering
choices.explanation: Incorrect — VPC Peering connects VPCs to each other, not to AWS services.

choices.label: B
choices.text: VPC Endpoints
choices.explanation: Correct — VPC Endpoints allow private connectivity to AWS services without internet access.

choices.label: C
choices.text: NAT Gateway
choices.explanation: Incorrect — NAT Gateway provides internet access for private subnets, not direct service connectivity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Internet Gateway
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Internet Gateway provides internet access, not private service connectivity.

questions.question: A company wants to implement health checks and automatic failover for their application. Which AWS service should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CloudWatch alarms only
choices.explanation: Incorrect — CloudWatch alarms monitor but don't provide automatic failover capabilities.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Route 53 health checks with failover
choices.explanation: Correct — Route 53 health checks can monitor application health and automatically failover to backup resources.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Auto Scaling groups only
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Auto Scaling groups manage capacity but don't provide health check-based failover.

choices.label: D
choices.text: S3 static website hosting
choices.explanation: Incorrect — S3 static hosting doesn't provide health checks or failover capabilities.

questions.question: A company wants to distribute traffic across multiple targets with advanced routing capabilities. Which load balancer should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Network Load Balancer (NLB)
choices.explanation: Incorrect — NLB operates at Layer 4 and doesn't provide advanced application-level routing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Application Load Balancer (ALB)
choices.explanation: Correct — ALB operates at Layer 7 and provides advanced routing based on content, headers, and other application-level criteria.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Classic Load Balancer (CLB)
choices.explanation: Incorrect — CLB is legacy and has limited routing capabilities compared to ALB.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)
choices.explanation: Incorrect — GWLB is designed for third-party virtual appliances, not application traffic distribution.

questions.question: A company wants to design a stateless application architecture. Which approach should they implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Store session data in local memory
choices.explanation: Incorrect — storing session data locally makes the application stateful and reduces scalability.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use external session storage (ElastiCache, DynamoDB)
choices.explanation: Correct — external session storage allows any instance to handle requests, making the application stateless and scalable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use sticky sessions with load balancers
choices.explanation: Incorrect — sticky sessions create stateful behavior and reduce fault tolerance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Store user data in application code
choices.explanation: Incorrect — storing user data in application code creates stateful behavior and reduces scalability.

questions.question: A company wants to optimize their EC2 instances for compute-intensive workloads. Which instance family should they choose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: T3 instances
choices.explanation: Incorrect — T3 instances are burstable performance instances, not optimized for sustained compute-intensive workloads.

choices.label: B
choices.text: C5 instances
choices.explanation: Correct — C5 instances are compute-optimized with high CPU-to-memory ratio, ideal for compute-intensive workloads.

choices.label: C
choices.text: M5 instances
choices.explanation: Incorrect — M5 instances are general-purpose, not specifically optimized for compute-intensive workloads.

choices.label: D
choices.text: R5 instances
choices.explanation: Incorrect — R5 instances are memory-optimized, not compute-optimized.

questions.question: A company wants to run containerized applications without managing the underlying infrastructure. Which AWS service should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ECS with EC2 launch type
choices.explanation: Incorrect — ECS with EC2 requires managing the underlying EC2 instances.

choices.label: B
choices.text: ECS with Fargate
choices.explanation: Correct — ECS with Fargate provides serverless containers without managing underlying infrastructure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: EC2 with Docker
choices.explanation: Incorrect — EC2 with Docker requires managing the EC2 instances and container orchestration.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lambda functions
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Lambda is for serverless functions, not containerized applications.

questions.question: A company wants to track costs across multiple AWS accounts and services. Which approach should they implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use individual billing for each account
choices.explanation: Incorrect — individual billing makes it difficult to track costs across accounts and services.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Implement AWS Organizations with consolidated billing and cost allocation tags
choices.explanation: Correct — AWS Organizations provides consolidated billing and cost allocation tags enable tracking costs across accounts and services.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use CloudWatch for cost monitoring only
choices.explanation: Incorrect — CloudWatch monitors resources but doesn't provide comprehensive cost allocation across accounts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Manually track costs in spreadsheets
choices.explanation: Incorrect — manual tracking is error-prone and doesn't scale with multiple accounts.

questions.question: A company wants to optimize costs for variable workloads that can tolerate interruptions. Which pricing model should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: On-Demand instances
choices.explanation: Incorrect — On-Demand is the most expensive option and not cost-optimized for variable workloads.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Spot Instances
choices.explanation: Correct — Spot Instances provide up to 90% cost savings for workloads that can tolerate interruptions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reserved Instances
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Reserved Instances are for predictable workloads, not variable workloads.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dedicated Hosts
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Dedicated Hosts are the most expensive option and not suitable for variable workloads.

questions.question: A company wants to optimize Lambda costs by adjusting memory allocation. Which approach should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use maximum memory for all functions
choices.explanation: Incorrect — maximum memory increases costs unnecessarily for functions that don't need it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Right-size memory based on function requirements and monitor performance
choices.explanation: Correct — right-sizing memory allocation optimizes both performance and cost for Lambda functions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use minimum memory for all functions
choices.explanation: Incorrect — minimum memory may cause performance issues and timeouts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set memory based on function duration only
choices.explanation: Incorrect — memory should be based on actual resource requirements, not just duration.

questions.question: A company wants to reduce data transfer costs for S3 access from their VPC. Which solution should they implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use NAT Gateway for all S3 access
choices.explanation: Incorrect — NAT Gateway adds costs and doesn't reduce data transfer costs for S3.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use VPC Endpoints for S3 access
choices.explanation: Correct — VPC Endpoints keep S3 traffic within the AWS network, reducing data transfer costs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use Direct Connect for S3 access
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Direct Connect is expensive and not cost-effective for S3 access.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use Internet Gateway for S3 access
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Internet Gateway doesn't reduce data transfer costs and may increase them.

questions.question: A company wants to implement automatic cost monitoring and alerting. Which AWS service should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CloudWatch only
choices.explanation: Incorrect — CloudWatch monitors resources but doesn't provide comprehensive cost monitoring.

choices.label: B
choices.text: AWS Budgets with Cost Explorer
choices.explanation: Correct — AWS Budgets provides cost monitoring and alerting, while Cost Explorer provides detailed cost analysis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: S3 with cost reports
choices.explanation: Incorrect — S3 can store cost reports but doesn't provide real-time monitoring and alerting.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lambda functions for cost calculation
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Lambda functions would require custom development and don't provide built-in cost monitoring.

questions.question: A company wants to implement multi-factor authentication for their AWS accounts. Which approach should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use only IAM policies for access control
choices.explanation: Incorrect — IAM policies alone don't provide multi-factor authentication.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable MFA for root user and IAM users
choices.explanation: Correct — MFA should be enabled for both root user and IAM users to add an extra layer of security.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use only access keys for authentication
choices.explanation: Incorrect — access keys alone don't provide multi-factor authentication.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use only password policies
choices.explanation: Incorrect — password policies alone don't provide multi-factor authentication.

questions.question: A company wants to monitor and log API calls made to their AWS services. Which service should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CloudWatch only
choices.explanation: Incorrect — CloudWatch monitors resources but doesn't log API calls.

choices.label: B
choices.text: AWS CloudTrail
choices.explanation: Correct — CloudTrail logs API calls and provides audit trail for AWS services.

choices.label: C
choices.text: S3 access logs
choices.explanation: Incorrect — S3 access logs only track S3 access, not all AWS API calls.

choices.label: D
choices.text: VPC Flow Logs
choices.explanation: Incorrect — VPC Flow Logs track network traffic, not API calls.

questions.question: A company wants to detect malicious activity and potential security threats in their AWS environment. Which service should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AWS Config
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Config monitors resource compliance but doesn't detect security threats.

choices.label: B
choices.text: AWS GuardDuty
choices.explanation: Correct — GuardDuty uses machine learning to detect malicious activity and security threats.

choices.label: C
choices.text: CloudWatch alarms
choices.explanation: Incorrect — CloudWatch alarms monitor metrics but don't detect security threats.

choices.label: D
choices.text: S3 bucket policies
choices.explanation: Incorrect — S3 bucket policies control access but don't detect security threats.

questions.question: A company wants to encrypt their RDS database at rest. Which approach should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use only application-level encryption

questions.question: A company wants to implement an active-passive disaster recovery strategy. Which approach should they use?

choices.explanation: Correct — active-passive keeps standby resources ready for failover when primary fails.

choices.label: C

choices.explanation: Incorrect — this doesn't provide active-passive disaster recovery.

choices.label: D

choices.explanation: Incorrect — Multi-AZ provides high availability within region, not cross-region disaster recovery.

questions.question: A company wants to implement cross-region replication for their DynamoDB tables. Which approach should they use?

questions.question: A company wants to understand IAM policy evaluation logic. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: IAM policies are evaluated in random order

choices.label: B

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use only NAT Gateway for all outbound traffic
choices.explanation: Incorrect — NAT Gateway may introduce latency and doesn't optimize VPC performance.

questions.question: A company wants to optimize network throughput and bandwidth. Which approach should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use only default instance network performance
choices.explanation: Incorrect — default settings may not provide optimal network performance for high-throughput workloads.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use instance types with enhanced networking, placement groups, and optimize network interface configuration
choices.explanation: Correct — network throughput optimization includes using instance types with enhanced networking, placement groups for low latency, and proper network interface configuration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use only S3 for all data transfer
choices.explanation: Incorrect — S3 is for object storage, not for optimizing network throughput.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use only CloudFront for all network optimization
choices.explanation: Incorrect — CloudFront is for content delivery, not for general network throughput optimization.

questions.question: A company wants to implement Reserved capacity planning. Which approach should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use only On-Demand instances without planning
choices.explanation: Incorrect — On-Demand instances are the most expensive option and don't provide cost savings.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Analyze usage patterns and purchase Reserved Instances for predictable workloads
choices.explanation: Correct — Reserved capacity planning involves analyzing usage patterns and purchasing RIs for predictable workloads to achieve significant cost savings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use only Spot Instances for all workloads
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Spot Instances can be interrupted and aren't suitable for all workloads.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use only manual capacity management
choices.explanation: Incorrect — manual management doesn't scale and doesn't provide cost optimization.

questions.question: A company wants to implement compute optimization strategies. Which approach should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use only the largest instance types for all workloads
choices.explanation: Incorrect — oversized instances waste money and don't provide cost optimization.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Right-size instances based on utilization metrics and use Auto Scaling for variable workloads
choices.explanation: Correct — compute optimization involves right-sizing instances based on actual utilization and using Auto Scaling to match capacity with demand.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use only Lambda for all compute needs
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Lambda is suitable for event-driven workloads but not for all compute requirements.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use only manual instance management
choices.explanation: Incorrect — manual management doesn't scale and doesn't provide optimal cost efficiency.

questions.question: A company wants to implement data transfer optimization. Which approach should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use only internet for all data transfer
choices.explanation: Incorrect — internet transfer is more expensive than AWS internal network transfer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use VPC endpoints, Direct Connect, and optimize data transfer patterns
choices.explanation: Correct — data transfer optimization includes using VPC endpoints for AWS services, Direct Connect for large data transfers, and optimizing transfer patterns to reduce costs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use only S3 for all data storage
choices.explanation: Incorrect — S3 is for storage, not for optimizing data transfer costs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use only manual data synchronization
choices.explanation: Incorrect — manual synchronization doesn't optimize data transfer costs.

questions.question: A company wants to implement resource sharing strategies. Which approach should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy resources separately in each account without sharing
choices.explanation: Incorrect — separate deployments increase costs and don't leverage resource sharing benefits.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use AWS Organizations with shared services and cross-account resource sharing
choices.explanation: Correct — resource sharing strategies include using AWS Organizations with shared services accounts and cross-account resource sharing to reduce costs and improve efficiency.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use only VPC peering for all connectivity
choices.explanation: Incorrect — VPC peering doesn't provide resource sharing capabilities.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use only S3 for all shared data
choices.explanation: Incorrect — S3 is for data storage, not for comprehensive resource sharing strategies.

questions.question: A company wants to implement comprehensive cost optimization across their AWS environment. Which approach should they use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use only manual cost tracking and optimization
choices.explanation: Incorrect — manual optimization doesn't scale and doesn't provide real-time cost management.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Implement AWS Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets, cost allocation tags, and automated optimization recommendations
choices.explanation: Correct — comprehensive cost optimization includes using AWS Cost Explorer for analysis, AWS Budgets for monitoring, cost allocation tags for tracking, and automated optimization recommendations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use only CloudWatch for cost monitoring
choices.explanation: Incorrect — CloudWatch monitors resources but doesn't provide comprehensive cost optimization capabilities.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use only On-Demand instances for all workloads
choices.explanation: Incorrect — On-Demand instances are the most expensive option and don't provide cost optimization.
